key_insight: A low-dimensional variational quantum circuit head can provide architectural robustness to label noise in medical image classification without explicit noise-handling tricks.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a hybrid quantum-classical design pattern for robust classifiers when training labels are unreliable, while still scaling from high-resolution RGB inputs via a frozen vision backbone.
method: Freeze an ImageNet-pretrained ViT-B/16 backbone and extract features from 224×224 RGB medical images.
Pass features through a trainable linear bottleneck and an eight-qubit variational quantum circuit with angle encoding and a linear cost function.
Compare against a ReLU head using the same backbone, bottleneck, parameter count, and optimizer under clean and noisy labels.
evidence_signal: Across six MedMNISTv2 benchmarks, the model led five on clean labels and remained stronger than many quantum and noise-robust classical baselines at 30% and 50% symmetric label noise.
watch_item: The approach depends on a frozen pretrained backbone and a small-qubit circuit, so hardware noise, circuit scaling, and transfer to other domains may limit practical gains.
paper_title: Architectural Robustness to Label Noise Using Variational Quantum Circuits for Medical Image Classification
